title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of John Wesley's sermon, The First-Fruits of the Spirit. It is the sermon as printed in John Wesley's 1771 Works. Rendered in modern English.
There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk after the flesh, but after the Spirit (Romans 8:1). Romans 8:1.

title: Those who truly believe
english: By those who are in Christ Jesus, Saint Paul plainly means those who truly believe in him. He means those who, being justified by faith, have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. Those who believe in this way no longer walk after the flesh. They no longer follow the motions of corrupt nature, but after the Spirit. Both their thoughts, words, and works are under the direction of the blessed Spirit of God.

title: No condemnation from God or from within
english: There is therefore now no condemnation to these. There is no condemnation to them from God, for he has justified them freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in Jesus. He has forgiven all their iniquities, and blotted out all their sins.

And there is no condemnation to them from within. For they have received, not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is of God, so that they might know the things which are freely given to them of God. And that Spirit bears witness with their spirits that they are the children of God. The note there is 1 Corinthians 2:12.

To this is added the testimony of their conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, they have lived their life in the world. The note there is 2 Corinthians 1:12.

title: A text often wrested
english: But this scripture has been misunderstood so often, and in so dangerous a manner. Such multitudes of unlearned and unstable men have wrested it to their own destruction. I set the Greek beside them. It names them as men untaught of God, and consequently unestablished in the truth which is after godliness.

I propose to show, as clearly as I can, first, who those are who are in Christ Jesus, and who do not walk after the flesh, but after the Spirit. And secondly, how there is no condemnation to these. I shall conclude with some practical inferences.

title: Who are in Christ Jesus
english: First, I am to show who those are that are in Christ Jesus. Are they not those who believe in his name? Those who are found in him, not having their own righteousness, but the righteousness which is of God by faith?

These, who have redemption through his blood, are properly said to be in him. For they dwell in Christ, and Christ in them. They are joined to the Lord in one Spirit. They are grafted into him as branches into the vine. They are united, as members to their head, in a manner which words cannot express, nor could it before enter into their hearts to conceive.

title: They do not walk after the flesh
english: Now whoever abides in him does not sin, and does not walk after the flesh. The flesh, in the usual language of Saint Paul, means corrupt nature. In this sense he uses the word, writing to the Galatians. The works of the flesh are manifest. Galatians 5:19.
And a little before that, he says, Walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfill the lust, or desire, of the flesh (Galatians 5:16). Galatians 5:16.

To prove that point, namely, that those who walk by the Spirit do not fulfill the lust of the flesh, he immediately adds this. The flesh lusts against the Spirit, but the Spirit lusts against the flesh, for these are contrary to each other, so that you may not do the things which you would.

That is the literal translation of his Greek. It is not, so that you cannot do the things that you would, as if the flesh overcame the Spirit. A translation like that has nothing to do with the original text of the apostle. It also makes his whole argument worth nothing. Yes, it asserts just the reverse of what he is proving.

title: They have crucified the flesh
english: Those who are of Christ, who abide in him, have crucified the flesh with its affections and lusts. They abstain from all those works of the flesh. They abstain from adultery and fornication, from uncleanness and lasciviousness, from idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, and variance. They abstain from emulations, wrath, strife, sedition, heresies, envyings, murders, drunkenness, and revelings. They abstain from every design, and word, and work to which the corruption of nature leads.

Although they feel the root of bitterness in themselves, yet they are endued with power from on high to trample it continually under foot, so that it cannot spring up to trouble them. So much so, that every fresh assault which they undergo only gives them fresh occasion of praise, of crying out, Thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through Jesus Christ our Lord.

title: In heart and in conduct
english: They now walk after the Spirit, both in their hearts and in their lives. They are taught by him to love God and their neighbor, with a love which is as a well of water, springing up into everlasting life. And by him they are led into every holy desire, into every divine and heavenly temper, until every thought which arises in their heart is holiness to the Lord.

Those who walk after the Spirit are also led by him into all holiness of conduct. Their speech is always in grace, seasoned with salt, with the love and fear of God. No corrupt communication comes out of their mouth, but only that which is good, that which is to the use of edifying, which is fit to minister grace to the hearers (Ephesians 4:29).

And in this, likewise, they exercise themselves day and night, to do only the things which please God. In all their outward behavior they follow him who left us an example, that we might tread in his steps. In all their dealings with their neighbor they walk in justice, mercy, and truth. And whatever they do, in every circumstance of life, they do all to the glory of God.

title: The fruits of the Spirit
english: These are the ones who indeed walk after the Spirit. Being filled with faith and with the Holy Ghost, they possess in their hearts, and show forth in their lives, in the whole course of their words and actions, the genuine fruits of the Spirit of God. Those fruits are love, joy, peace, long-suffering, gentleness, goodness, fidelity, meekness, temperance, and whatever else is lovely or praiseworthy.
They adorn in all things the gospel of God our Savior. And they give full proof to all mankind that they are indeed actuated by the same Spirit which raised Jesus from the dead.

title: No condemnation for past sins
english: I proposed to show, in the second place, how there is no condemnation to those who are thus in Christ Jesus, and who thus walk, not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

And first, to believers in Christ who walk in this way, there is no condemnation on account of their past sins. God does not condemn them for any of these. They are as though they had never been. They are cast as a stone into the depth of the sea, and he remembers them no more.

God, having set forth his Son to be a propitiation for them, through faith in his blood, has declared to them his righteousness, for the remission of the sins that are past. He therefore lays none of these to their charge. Their memorial has perished with them.

title: No condemnation in their own breast
english: And there is no condemnation in their own breast, no sense of guilt, or dread of the wrath of God. They have the witness in themselves. They are conscious of their part in the blood of sprinkling. They have not received again the spirit of bondage to fear, to doubt and racking uncertainty. But they have received the Spirit of adoption, crying in their hearts, Abba, Father.
Thus, being justified by faith, they have the peace of God ruling in their hearts. It flows from a continual sense of his pardoning mercy, and from the answer of a good conscience toward God.

title: If the light of faith is lost
english: If it is said that sometimes a believer in Christ may lose his sight of the mercy of God, that sometimes such darkness may fall upon him that he no longer sees him who is invisible, and no longer feels that witness in himself of his part in the atoning blood, and that then he is inwardly condemned, and again has the sentence of death in himself, I answer.

Suppose it is so. Suppose he does not see the mercy of God. Then he is not a believer. For faith implies light, the light of God shining upon the soul. So far, therefore, as anyone loses this light, he for the time loses his faith.
And no doubt a true believer in Christ may lose the light of faith. And so far as this is lost, he may for a time fall again into condemnation.

But this is not the case of those who now are in Christ Jesus, who now believe in his name. For so long as they believe, and walk after the Spirit, neither God condemns them, nor does their own heart.

title: Not condemned for present sins
english: They are not condemned, secondly, for any present sins, for now transgressing the commandments of God. For they do not transgress them. They do not walk after the flesh, but after the Spirit. This is the continual proof of their love of God, that they keep his commandments.

Even as Saint John bears witness: Whoever is born of God does not commit sin. For his seed remains in him, and he cannot sin, because he is born of God. He cannot, so long as that seed of God, that loving, holy faith, remains in him. So long as he keeps himself in this, that wicked one does not touch him.

Now it is plain he is not condemned for the sins which he does not commit at all. Those, therefore, who are thus led by the Spirit are not under the law. Galatians 5:18. They are not under the curse or condemnation of it, for it condemns none but those who break it. Thus that law of God, You shall not steal, condemns none but those who do steal. Thus, Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, condemns only those who do not keep it holy.

But against the fruits of the Spirit there is no law. Galatians 5:23. The apostle declares this more fully in those memorable words of his former letter to Timothy. We know that the law is good, if a man uses it lawfully, knowing this. If, while he uses the law of God, in order either to convince or to direct, he knows and remembers this.

He then quotes the Greek. The sense is not that the law is not made for a righteous man, but that the law does not lie against a righteous man. It has no force against him, no power to condemn him. But it lies against the lawless and disobedient, against the ungodly and sinners, against the unholy and profane, according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God. 1 Timothy 1:8-9, 11.

title: Inward sin still remains
english: They are not condemned, thirdly, for inward sin, even though it does now remain. That the corruption of nature does still remain, even in those who are the children of God by faith, that they have in them the seeds of pride and vanity, of anger, lust, and evil desire, yes, sin of every kind, is too plain to be denied. It is a matter of daily experience.

And on this account Saint Paul speaks to those whom he had just before witnessed to be in Christ Jesus. The note is 1 Corinthians 1:2. He speaks to them as called of God into the fellowship, or participation, of his Son Jesus Christ. The note is 1 Corinthians 1:9. Yet he declares: Brothers, I could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to carnal people, even as to babes in Christ. 1 Corinthians 3:1.
Babes in Christ. So we see they were in Christ. They were believers in a low degree. And yet how much sin remained in them, of that carnal mind which is not subject to the law of God?

title: They do not yield to it
english: And yet, for all this, they are not condemned. Although they feel the flesh, the evil nature in them, although they are more aware day by day that their heart is deceitful and desperately wicked, yet so long as they do not yield to it, so long as they give no place to the devil, so long as they maintain a continual war with all sin, with pride, anger, and desire, so that the flesh has no dominion over them, but they still walk after the Spirit, there is no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus.
God is well pleased with their sincere, though imperfect, obedience. And they have confidence toward God, knowing they are his, by the Spirit which he has given them. 1 John 3:24.

title: Sin cleaving to all they do
english: Fourthly, they are continually convinced of sin cleaving to all they do. They are conscious of not fulfilling the perfect law, either in their thoughts, or words, or works. They know they do not love the Lord their God with all their heart, and mind, and soul, and strength. They feel more or less of pride or self-will stealing in and mixing with their best duties.

Even in their more immediate communion with God, when they assemble themselves with the great congregation, and when they pour out their souls in secret to him who sees all the thoughts and intents of the heart, they are continually ashamed of their wandering thoughts, or of the deadness and dullness of their affections. Yet there is no condemnation to them still, either from God or from their own heart.

The thought of these many defects only gives them a deeper sense that they always need that blood of sprinkling, which speaks for them in the ears of God, and that Advocate with the Father who ever lives to make intercession for them. So far are these from driving them away from him in whom they have believed, that they rather drive them the closer to him, whom they feel the want of every moment.
And at the same time, the deeper sense they have of this want, the more earnest desire they feel, and the more diligent they are, as they have received the Lord Jesus, so to walk in him.

title: Sins of infirmity
english: They are not condemned, fifthly, for sins of infirmity, as they are usually called. Perhaps it would be advisable rather to call them infirmities, so that we may not seem to give any approval to sin, or to lessen it in any degree, by thus coupling it with infirmity. But if we must keep so ambiguous and dangerous an expression, by sins of infirmity I mean such involuntary failings as saying a thing we believe true, though in fact it proves false, or hurting our neighbor without knowing or intending it, perhaps when we meant to do him good.

Though these are deviations from the holy, and acceptable, and perfect will of God, yet they are not properly sins. Nor do they bring any guilt on the conscience of those who are in Christ Jesus. They do not separate between God and them, neither do they intercept the light of his countenance, as being in no way inconsistent with their general character of walking, not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

title: What they cannot help
english: Lastly, there is no condemnation to them for anything whatever which it is not in their power to help, whether it is of an inward or outward nature, and whether it is doing something or leaving something undone.

For instance, the Lord's Supper is to be administered. But you do not partake of it. Why do you not? You are confined by sickness. Therefore you cannot help omitting it, and for the same reason you are not condemned.
There is no guilt, because there is no choice. As there is a willing mind, it is accepted according to what a man has, not according to what he does not have.

A believer may indeed sometimes be grieved, because he cannot do what his soul longs for. He may cry out, when he is detained from worshiping God in the great congregation: Like as the hart pants after the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, O God. My soul is thirsty for God, yes, even for the living God. When shall I come to appear in the presence of God?

He may earnestly desire, only still saying in his heart, not as I will, but as you will, to go again with the multitude and bring them forth into the house of God. But still, if he cannot go, he feels no condemnation, no guilt, no sense of God's displeasure. He can cheerfully yield up those desires, with these words: O my soul, put your trust in God, for I will yet give him thanks, who is the help of my countenance and my God.

title: Sins of surprise
english: It is more difficult to determine concerning those which are usually called sins of surprise. For example, one who commonly possesses his soul in patience, on a sudden and violent temptation, speaks or acts in a manner not consistent with the royal law, You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

Perhaps it is not easy to fix a general rule concerning transgressions of this nature. We cannot say either that men are, or that they are not, condemned for sins of surprise in general. But it seems, whenever a believer is overtaken by surprise in a fault, there is more or less condemnation, as there is more or less concurrence of his will. In proportion as a sinful desire, or word, or action is more or less voluntary, so we may conceive God is more or less displeased, and there is more or less guilt upon the soul.

title: When surprise is no excuse
english: But if so, then there may be some sins of surprise which bring much guilt and condemnation. For in some instances, our being surprised is owing to some willful and culpable neglect, or to a sleepiness of soul which might have been prevented, or shaken off, before the temptation came.

A man may be warned beforehand, either by God or by man, that trials and danger are at hand, and yet may say in his heart, A little more slumber, a little more folding of the hands to rest. Now if such a one afterward falls, though unawares, into the snare which he might have avoided, that he fell unawares is no excuse. He might have foreseen, and have shunned, the danger.
The falling, even by surprise, in such an instance as this, is in effect a willful sin. And as such, it must expose the sinner to condemnation, both from God and from his own conscience.

title: When the will hardly consents
english: On the other hand, there may be sudden assaults, either from the world, or the God of this world, and frequently from our own evil hearts, which we did not, and hardly could, foresee. And by these even a believer, while weak in faith, may possibly be borne down, suppose into a degree of anger, or thinking evil of another, with scarce any concurrence of his will.

Now in such a case, the jealous God would undoubtedly show him that he had done foolishly. He would be convinced of having swerved from the perfect law, from the mind which was in Christ, and consequently grieved with a godly sorrow, and lovingly ashamed before God. Yet he need not come into condemnation.

God does not lay folly to his charge, but has compassion upon him, even as a Father pities his own children. And his heart does not condemn him. In the midst of that sorrow and shame he can still say, I will trust and not be afraid. For the Lord Jehovah is my strength and my song. He also has become my salvation.

title: Why fear for past sin
english: It remains only to draw some practical inferences from the preceding considerations. And first, if there is no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, and do not walk after the flesh but after the Spirit, on account of their past sin, then why are you fearful, O you of little faith?

Though your sins were once more in number than the sand, what is that to you, now you are in Christ Jesus? Who shall lay anything to the charge of God's elect? It is God who justifies. Who is he that condemns? All the sins you have committed, from your youth up until the hour when you were accepted in the Beloved, are driven away as chaff. They are gone, they are lost, swallowed up, remembered no more.

You are now born of the Spirit. Will you be troubled or afraid for what was done before you were born? Away with your fears. You are not called to fear, but to the Spirit of love and of a sound mind. Know your calling. Rejoice in God your Savior, and give thanks to God your Father through him.

title: If you have sinned again
english: Will you say, But I have again committed sin, since I had redemption through his blood? And therefore it is that I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes. It is fitting that you should abhor yourself, and it is God who has worked you to this very same thing. But do you now believe? Has he again enabled you to say, I know that my Redeemer lives, and the life which I now live, I live by faith in the Son of God? Then that faith again cancels all that is past, and there is no condemnation to you.

At whatever time you truly believe in the name of the Son of God, all your sins before that hour vanish away as the morning dew. Now then, stand fast in the liberty with which Christ has made you free. He has once more made you free from the power of sin, as well as from the guilt and punishment of it. Do not be entangled again with the yoke of bondage. Neither the vile, devilish bondage of sin, of evil desires, evil tempers, or words, or works, the most grievous yoke on this side hell, nor the bondage of slavish, tormenting fear, of guilt and self-condemnation.

title: Whoever commits sin now
english: But secondly, do all who abide in Christ Jesus not walk after the flesh, but after the Spirit? Then we cannot but infer that whoever now commits sin has no part or lot in this matter. He is even now condemned by his own heart. But if our heart condemns us, if our own conscience bears witness that we are guilty, undoubtedly God does also. For he is greater than our heart, and knows all things (1 John 3:20), so that we cannot deceive him, if we can deceive ourselves.

And do not think to say, I was justified once. My sins were once forgiven me. I do not know that. Neither will I dispute whether they were or not. Perhaps, at this distance of time, it is next to impossible to know, with any tolerable degree of certainty, whether that was a true, genuine work of God, or whether you did only deceive your own soul.
But this I know, with the utmost degree of certainty. He who commits sin is of the devil. Therefore you are of your father the devil. It cannot be denied, for you do the works of your father.
Do not flatter yourself with vain hopes. Do not say to your soul, Peace, peace. For there is no peace. Cry aloud. Cry to God out of the deep, if perhaps he may hear your voice.

Come to him as at the first, as wretched and poor, as sinful, miserable, blind, and naked. And beware that you do not allow your soul to take any rest, until his pardoning love is again revealed, until he heals your backslidings, and fills you again with the faith that works by love.

title: Do not fret over inward sin
english: Thirdly, is there no condemnation to those who walk after the Spirit, by reason of inward sin still remaining, so long as they do not give way to it, nor by reason of sin cleaving to all they do? Then do not fret yourself because of ungodliness, though it still remains in your heart. Do not complain because you still come short of the glorious image of God, nor yet because pride, self-will, or unbelief cleave to all your words and works.

And do not be afraid to know all the evil of your heart, to know yourself as you also are known. Yes, desire of God that you may not think of yourself more highly than you ought to think. Let your continual prayer be:
Show me, as my soul can bear, the depth of inbred sin. All the unbelief declare, the pride that lurks within.

But when he hears your prayer, and unveils your heart, when he shows you thoroughly what spirit you are of, then beware that your faith does not fail you, that you do not allow your shield to be torn from you. Be abased. Be humbled in the dust. See yourself nothing, less than nothing and vanity. But still, do not let your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
Still hold fast: I, even I, have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. And as the heavens are higher than the earth, so is his love higher than even my sins.

Therefore God is merciful to you, a sinner. Such a sinner as you are. God is love, and Christ has died. Therefore the Father himself loves you. You are his child. Therefore he will withhold from you no manner of thing that is good.
Is it good that the whole body of sin, which is now crucified in you, should be destroyed? It shall be done. You shall be cleansed from all filthiness, both of flesh and spirit.

Is it good that nothing should remain in your heart but the pure love of God alone? Be of good cheer. You shall love the Lord your God, with all your heart, and mind, and soul, and strength. Faithful is he who has promised, who also will do it.

It is your part, patiently to continue in the work of faith, and in the labor of love, and in cheerful peace, in humble confidence, with calm and resigned, and yet earnest expectation, to wait until the zeal of the Lord of Hosts shall perform this.

title: Weakness and infirmities
english: Fourthly, if those who are in Christ, and walk after the Spirit, are not condemned for sins of infirmity, as neither for involuntary failings, nor for anything whatever which they are not able to help, then beware, O you who have faith in his blood, that Satan herein gain no advantage over you.

You are still foolish and weak, blind and ignorant, weaker than any words can express, more foolish than it can yet enter into your heart to conceive, knowing nothing yet as you ought to know. Yet do not let all your weakness and folly, or any fruit of it which you are not yet able to avoid, shake your faith, your trust in God as his child, or disturb your peace or joy in the Lord.
The rule which some give as to willful sins, and which in that case may perhaps be dangerous, is undoubtedly wise and safe if it is applied only to the case of weakness and infirmities.

Have you fallen, O man of God? Yet do not lie there, fretting yourself and bemoaning your weakness. But meekly say, Lord, I shall fall thus every moment, unless you uphold me with your hand. And then arise. Leap and walk. Go on your way, and run with patience the race set before you.

title: If you are overtaken in a fault
english: Lastly, since a believer need not come into condemnation, even though he is surprised into what his soul abhors, supposing his being surprised is not owing to any carelessness or willful neglect of his own, if you who believe are thus overtaken in a fault, then grieve to the Lord. It shall be a precious balm. Pour out your heart before him, and show him your trouble.

And pray with all your might to him who is touched with the feeling of your infirmities, that he would establish, and strengthen, and settle your soul, and not allow you to fall any more. But still he does not condemn you. Why should you fear? You have no need of any fear that has torment. You shall love him who loves you, and that is enough. More love will bring more strength.

And as soon as you love him with all your heart, you shall be perfect and entire, lacking nothing. Wait in peace for that hour when the God of peace shall sanctify you wholly, so that your whole spirit, and soul, and body may be preserved blameless until the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
